previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma and a history of biliary stents and recurrent infections, was admitted with fever, chills, and lack of output from his percutaneous biliary drain, consistent with cholangitis and early sepsis. On admission, he underwent percutaneous balloon dilation and exchange of his biliary drain. Blood cultures grew E. coli, prompting a switch to IV meropenem. An MRCP showed signs of cholangitis and biliary stenosis, leading to an ERCP for clearance of sludge and debris from the stents. His biliary drain was subsequently capped, and he improved clinically with normalized liver enzymes and resolution of fever. He was diagnosed with bacteremia and newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, managed with insulin and diet. He was discharged home with a plan for 10 days of IV meropenem via home health, prophylactic oral vancomycin, and follow-up for liver tests and oncology care.

Areas of linear bibasilar atelectasis/ scarring are seen without definite

and mediastinal silhouettes are stable.  Right upper lobe calcified granuloma
is re- demonstrated..  Pulmonary nodules 4 mm and smaller seen on prior chest
CT from ___ or better appreciated on CT.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute cardiopulmonary process.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with cholangiocarcinoma w/PTBD and perc chole
tubes p/w fever, pain, rising tbili  // cholangiogram +/- exchange of
catheters

COMPARISON:
Procedure from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ radiologist performed the
procedure.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
25 mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 25 min during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site
MEDICATIONS: Fentanyl Versed
CONTRAST: 10 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  3.3 min, 10 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Cholangiogram through existing  percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage
access.
2. Exchange of the existing percutaneous trans-hepatic biliary drainage
catheter with a new 8 ___ modified the strong internal/external PTBD
catheter.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The right abdomen was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.
Initial scout images showed biliary drain in the appropriate position. The
right tube was injected with dilute contrast.  The percutaneous
cholecystostomy tube was also injected with diluted contrast.  The images were
stored on PACS.
Following the subcutaneous injection of 1% lidocaine and instillation of
lidocaine jelly into the skin site, the right catheter was cut and ___
wire was advanced through the catheter into the duodenum.  The catheter was
removed over the wire and a 8 ___ percutaneous trans hepatic biliary
drainage catheter was advanced into the duodenum. The wire and inner stiffener
were removed, the catheter was flushed attached to a bag and sterile dressings
were applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications.

FINDINGS:


1. Patent percutaneous cholecystostomy tube.
2. Cholangiogram showing obstruction of the distal segment of the internal/
external PTBD.
3. Successful exchange of existing percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage
catheters with new 8 ___ PTBD.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful exchange of existing percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage
catheters with new 8 ___ PTBD.  Catheters were attached to a bag for
external drainage.
